exercises.q: Нет ничего ___ (плохой) телемаркетинга.
exercises.why: In both English and Russian adjectives and adverbs have three forms, which are called degrees: positive, comparative, superlative — good, better, best; fast, faster, fastest. The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "-ее" (sometimes shortened to "-ей") to the stem of the adjective: новый — новее; красивый — красивее. This comparative form is the same for all genders and the plural. It is not declined and can be used as a predicate only. An adjective in the comparative degree may be followed by the object of comparison in the Genitive case, or by a phrase consisting of "чем" plus the object of comparison in the Nominative case: *Ваш автомобиль новее моего автомобиля.… — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 80–81.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
